extracted.intended_audience: adult basic education counselors, guidance instructors, paraprofessionals writing grant proposals
extracted.subtask_short: writing funding proposals for ABE projects
extracted.subtask_description: A practical instructional package teaching adult-education guidance staff how to prepare, format, and self-evaluate sample funding proposals and related research/evaluation designs for Adult Basic Education (ABE) guidance and counseling projects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Knowledge of ABE terminology
rubrics_metrics.description: The trainee will be able to define verbally and in writing frequently used terms in Adult Basic Education; demonstrate ability to define correctly from memory a high proportion of listed terms (preassessment: 3/4 correct; postassessment: 18/20 correct) and present an additional list of 10–20 terms used in ABE that they can defend to a supervisor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lists sample terms (e.g., Adult Basic Education, Adult High School Completion, non-reader, life career planning, units/credits). Learning activities: write definitions for the twenty preassessment terms, add 5–10 more, defend choices to supervisor. Use both oral and written demonstrations of mastery.

rubrics_metrics.name: Behavioral objectives: components
rubrics_metrics.description: A behavioral objective must include (I.a) a specific task (observable, measurable behavior), (II) conditions under which the task is to be accomplished, and (III) criteria providing standards of competence against which desired outcomes can be measured.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Checklist and example provided: 'The trainee will be able to write a behavioral objective, as a result of participating in a three-hour workshop. Evidence... when the trainee accurately rewrites eight out of ten inadequately stated objectives...'. Anti-patterns: vague objectives (e.g., 'will have improved attitude') are inadequate; objectives must be measurable and include task, conditions, criteria. Postassessment: write ten objectives including task, conditions, criteria; implement at least two in workplace and report results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research design essentials
rubrics_metrics.description: A research proposal must contain: a clear problem statement, unambiguous hypotheses, operational definitions, and a clearly stated research methodology.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommended readings listed (Isaac, Kerlinger, Van Dalen, Campbell). Learning activities include defining terms (control group, dependent/independent variables, randomization, pretest/posttest) and creating a formal research design that tests counselor effectiveness with specified design notation (R x y, etc.). Pre/postassessment: submit for approval a proposal with the listed elements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statement of Problem and Need
rubrics_metrics.description: The statement should be clear yet brief with definite conclusions; the significance of the problem must be specifically indicated and a sense of urgency created.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notes: describe who target groups are and the effects of the problem on them; explain why current systems are not meeting the needs; indicate plan for incorporating project after outside funding; identify professional and lay groups involved; include anticipated outcomes. Avoid ambiguous wording; clarify in operational terms and preview the approach.

rubrics_metrics.name: Objectives: clarity, measurability, and alignment
rubrics_metrics.description: Project objectives must be concise, quantifiable (measurable), realistic (doable), limited in number (not too many), and consistent with the problem statement and procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Separate objectives from procedures. Use agency language when appropriate. Types: general (goals) vs specific (measurable objectives); covert vs overt objectives (avoid self-serving covert ones). Verbs are important. Objectives should be testable and tied to evaluation measures. Recommendation: include 1–10 'group' goals plus sample enabling objectives; keep remainder on file.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedures/Project Methodology
rubrics_metrics.description: The procedures section is the primary basis for evaluating the proposal and must describe in detail the steps to be followed to achieve objectives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include: populations/samples/experimental and control groups (origin, composition, purpose, numbers), experimental design/methods, data-types and instruments (questionnaires, tests), analysis methods (statistical procedures), approximate time schedule, expected end-product (including final report). Provide flow charts, sequence of activities, and justify chosen procedures (including alternatives considered). Ensure activities map directly to objectives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Personnel
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify personnel (name, title) and give brief statements of pertinent experience for principal investigator and key staff, percent of time on project, and job descriptions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include resumes if personnel are known. For the budget, list salaries and fringe benefits separately and give percent time per position. Include consultants and indicate their roles and costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation: process and product tied to objectives
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe both process (how the project is carried out) and product (outcomes) evaluation and explicitly relate evaluation to stated objectives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluation should include institutional inventory (input), operational evaluation (implementation monitoring), and final/summative evaluation (outcome assessment). Spell out methods, timing, data handling/storage, who will evaluate, sampling techniques, auditing procedures if required, dissemination of results, and factors determining replicability. Each objective should have corresponding measurement procedures. Consider both objective and subjective measures; estimate expected outcome differential and, if useful, cost-effectiveness ratios.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget: completeness and realism
rubrics_metrics.description: Budgets must itemize personnel (salaries, percent time, fringe), consultants, travel/per diem, space costs/rentals, consumable supplies, equipment, other costs, indirect costs, and total costs; if multi-year, show separate columns per year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include organizational chart, specific staff requirements, job descriptions, and one-page resumes. Itemize travel (trips, miles, per-mile rates, per-diem days), list in-kind contributions with monetary value, and indicate sources/amounts of other funds. Caution: do not overbudget or 'pad' requests; ask for what you actually need. Consult finance officer if unsure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Format and presentation (style and form)
rubrics_metrics.description: First impressions matter: general appearance, neatness, consistency of style, and professional presentation (charts, maps, graphs, title page) are critical; proposals may be rejected on poor appearance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow a consistent typing/style manual; be meticulous with typing, proofreading, graphics. Consider hiring an artist for cover/charts if necessary. Ensure completeness and professionalism. Provide preliminaries (title page, table of contents, lists) followed by text and appendices in conventional order.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposal structure and required components
rubrics_metrics.description: A properly formatted proposal includes preliminaries (title page, table of contents, lists), the text (introduction with statement of problem, need, justification, related research, objectives, procedures, work plan, evaluation), reference materials, and appendices (agency forms, abstract, budget, personnel, figures).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Not every proposal includes all items; follow funder-specific instructions when available. The text typically begins with Chapter I and each major section should start on a new page. Include expected end-products and dissemination plans in the text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pagination, table of contents, and lists formatting
rubrics_metrics.description: Page numbering uses two series (small Roman numerals for preliminaries; Arabic numerals for main text). The title page and major section opening pages are counted but may not display numerals. Table of contents headings must match text exactly; use capitalization/indentation rules; list tables and figures with numbers and exact captions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Place page numbers four double spaces from top, right-aligned. Tables numbered with Roman numerals; Figures with Arabic numbers. Use leaders to guide eye to page numbers. Ensure consistency in heading styles and indentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Title selection
rubrics_metrics.description: Title should be brief, accurate, comprehensive, and phrased to include key words under which the project would be indexed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Effective titles are usually three or four words or groups of words; avoid grandiose or awkward phrasing; make meaning clear on first reading. Consider indexability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of clear, concise language and avoidance of jargon/bombast
rubrics_metrics.description: Write proposals in clear, concise language; avoid obscure technical terms, polysyllabic verbosity, pompous prose, and double entendres or profanity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notes humorously advise: 'DON'T USE BIG WORDS!' Ensure objectives are in measurable terms; write for a stranger to the program. Be prepared to negotiate after submission. 'Do your politics' within institutions and with funders. Recognize institution limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Problem identification: theoretical vs reality vs compromise level
rubrics_metrics.description: Problem identification should address theoretical considerations, real-world constraints, and a compromise level acceptable within socio-political and economic environments (institutional fit, support, funding/time considerations).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe problem straightforwardly, create urgency, identify specific needs, and clarify operational terms. Show that proposer has insight and knowledge to deliver product; preview approach in the problem statement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedures: flow, timeline and sequencing
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedures must indicate sequence of events, flow-charted steps, specific activities, time frame and work relationships, and external political processes where relevant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include starting dates, realistic timelines, flow charts indicating dependencies and estimated times, evidence of sequence clarity, and plans for dissemination and by-products. Provide sufficient time for data collection and final report.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation types and timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Distinguish evaluation types: context (relates to problem statement), implementation (checks whether plan is followed), process (checks progress toward objectives; formative), and outcome (summative; measures final attainment of objectives).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan for antecedent (input) measures, transaction (implementation) records, interim audits, terminal evaluation, and reporting of outcomes. Allow for revising objectives during developmental projects if justified by evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Auditing of evaluation
rubrics_metrics.description: If auditing is required, it should be delineated: auditing can duplicate evaluation, operate a different evaluation system for comparison, focus on the evaluation system itself, or combine functions—to validate the evaluation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note that auditing can be threatening to institutions; ensure proper handling, clarity of auditor roles, and consider costs and managerial implications. If guidelines call for auditing, budget for it and describe auditing methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Management design and project flow/network
rubrics_metrics.description: Develop a network-based flow diagram for project management that captures all procedures and events (e.g., project funded → director selected → staff selected → workshops → evaluator selected → data collection → termination).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Flow chart derived from procedures and evaluation design; circles = completed events; lines = activities. Add estimated times to show duration between events. Budget and resource planning should follow management design.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposal roles and functions
rubrics_metrics.description: A proposal serves multiple roles: planning document, formal funding request, negotiation document, legal document, operational guide, accountability document, and planning base for future proposals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Involve those who will implement the project in proposal development; ensure staff consent on problems, objectives, and procedures. Use proposal as foundation for conceptualization, fund allocation, operations, evaluation, contractual relationships and advocacy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appendices and supporting documentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Include appendices with agency forms, project abstract, budget, budget justification, personnel bios/resumes, and any required tables/figures or instruments (tests, questionnaires).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Put sample-proposal forms and instructions in appendices; include copies of instruments when required; provide final approval sheet and documentation of signatures/copies distribution as needed by institution/funder.

rubrics_metrics.name: Self-evaluation / proposal review checklist
rubrics_metrics.description: A writer's self-evaluation checklist covering General fit, Statement of the Problem, Related Research, Objectives, Procedure, Personnel, Evaluation, Budget, etc., with Yes/No items to determine readiness for submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Representative questions: 'Does the project fit within the grantor's guidelines? Have the evaluation procedures been considered? Does the proposal have continuity between sections? Is the proposal specific and detailed enough? Are objectives testable? Does the procedure identify population and variables? Are copies of instruments included?' Use the checklist to decide whether further development is needed before submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dissemination and replication planning
rubrics_metrics.description: Specify how evaluation materials and final results will be disseminated, who will receive them, and what factors determine whether the project can be replicated in another community.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include efforts for dissemination in procedures and evaluation sections; identify potential by-products and whether the sponsoring agency can continue activities after project end. Plan to indicate phases beyond year one and efforts for transfer or institutionalization.
